text:
The Rangers spent the hours before puck drop looking back. It was a hundred years to the night since the franchise's first game, played at Madison Square Garden against a team from Montreal, and the club marked it with a full pregame ceremony. Then Will Cuylle spent the second period making sure the centennial had a proper ending: two goals in nine minutes, the second while his team was killing a penalty, and a 3-1 win over the Canadiens that stretched New York's winning streak to three.

Montreal got there first. At 7:59 of the second, Phillip Danault tipped a Lane Hutson point shot past Joonas Korpisalo (enough of a deflection that, as The Hockey News' Karine Hains noted, even the Canadiens' own app first credited Noah Dobson). Cuylle answered 1:48 later, redirecting a Marcus Pettersson shot with J.T. Miller also assisting, and our win chances for the Rangers went from 32% to 52%. With 57 seconds left in the period and the Rangers short-handed, Adam Fox found him again and Cuylle beat Jacob Fowler with a wrister that carried only an 8% chance of going in. That one moved New York from 51% to 75%.

Scott Morrow added the third at 6:44 of the third period on a 2% shot, his first goal as a Ranger and the second of his career. It was the least likely goal of the night, and it mattered, because the Canadiens owned that period. They piled up 1.53 expected goals (the quality of their chances) in the third and finished with 58 shot attempts to 43. Korpisalo, back after a long stint on injured reserve, stopped 24 of 25 and saved 1.5 goals more than the shots deserved, including a 40% look from Juraj Slafkovský late in the third.

On the chances, Montreal had the better of it: 2.46 expected goals to 2.33, and our replays of every shot give the Canadiens the win 61% of the time. That will sting more because of the power play. The Canadiens went 0 for 4 with 0.13 expected goals, on the same day Nick Suzuki said the unit was "definitely not broken," as Sportsnet's Eric Engels pointed out. Fowler allowed three on 1.88 expected. Montreal still sits on 28 points, but a night like this is why the underlying numbers worry us more than the standings do.
headline: A hundred years in, Cuylle makes the night his
